 SCCH-25 2 MVC No.8019/2023  JUDGMENT

The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him and the damages suffered by his Bullock Cart in a road accident dated 01.09.2023.

Chikkaswamy vs K.S.R.T.C on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142660233/
1 2.
The case of the Petitioner in brief is that:

On 01.09.2023 at about 06.30am, while he was riding the Bullock Cart transporting Sugarcane to the factory from his village towards KM-Doddi on Maddur- Malavalli Main Road, near Mellahalli Village, Maddur Taluk, Mandya District, a KSRTC Bus bearing REg.No.KA-11-F-0411 driven by its driver with high speed in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life and dashed against the Cart.
Due to impact the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was shifted to KM Doddi Government Hospital, wherein he was given first aid treatment.
Later he was shifted to Mandya Govt. Hospital and admitted for one day and treated conservatively, now he is under follow- up treatment.

So far he has spent Rs.30,000/- towards hospital, medical expenses, food and nourishments,
conveyances, attendant charges and other incidental charges.

3. It is the further case of the petitioner that, in the said accident the bullocks were grievously injured and one of the bullock was not capable to do work due to injuries, hence the petitioner left it to GAU-Shala.
The cost of one bullock was Rs.40,000/- and also the bullock cart was completely damaged and the same was got repaired which incurred him a sum of Rs.38,350/- towards its repair.
Prior to the date of accident the petitioner was hale and healthy, doing Agriculture Work and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the impact of the accident, now he is not in a condition to do his normal routine activities as he was doing prior to the accident.
The KM Doddi Police registered a case in Cr.No.147/2023 p/u/Sec.279, 337 of IPC against the driver of the said KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-11-F- 0411 and later filed charge sheet.
The respondent being the RC owner is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
4. In response to notice issued by this Tribunal, the Respondent appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.
5. Objection of the Respondent.
The Respondent denied the averments made in the petition in Para 1 to 22.
Further it has denied the manner of accident and involvement of the bus in the accident.

Further stated that the KSRTC Bus driver drove the bus from Malavalli to Kalasipalya via KM Doddi, Maddur, Channapatna at Mellahalli bridge due to heavy rain and heavy traffic, at that time the petitioner's cart was heavily loaded with sugar cane and the cart dashed to the KSRTC Bus.
The accident occurred due to the sole negligence of the petitioner.
The KSRTC bus driver is not at all responsible for the said accident.
Further the Respondent denied the age, income, occupation of the petitioner and stated that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against them.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, the accident occurred on 01.09.2023 at about 6.30am due to rash and negligent of driving of driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Chikkaswamy vs K.S.R.T.C on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142660233/
2 Reg.No.KA-11-F-0411 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?

7. The Petitioner in order to prove his case, has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.12.

On the other side, the Respondent examined Mr. N.Nandhisha - Driver of the KSRTC Bus as RW.1 and got marked Exs.R.1 to R.5.
8.
Heard the arguments and perused the materials on record.

9. On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows:-
Issue No.1: In the affirmative, Issue No.2: In the affirmative, Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issue No.1:-

In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the Driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-11-F-0411, the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 by reiterating the petition averments in his chief examination affidavit and produced 5 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.5.
The Respondent has contended that the accident occurred due to sole negligence of the petitioner himself.
In the cross-examination of PW.1, he has stated that the accident occurred on Malavalli Maddur NH Road.
He purchased the Bullock Cart 2 to 3 years ago but, has not produced any bills.
He was earning about Rs.500/- to Rs.600/- per day from the Bullock Cart.
11. Ex.P.3 MVA report shows that there was damages to the vehicle bearing No.KA-11-F-0411 on the front windscreen glass, left headlight, indicator and front left bumper, body, grill damaged.

The petitioner has produced Ex.P.1 FIR in Cr.No.147/2023 of KM Doddi on the complaint of Mr.Sunil,
Ex.P.2 crime detail, vehicle seizure mahazar and Ex.P.5 charge sheet.
Upon appreciation of the said documents as above it is clear that there was sole negligence on the part of the Driver of the offending KSRTC Bus in causing the accident.

Further, the wound certificate produced by the Petitioner as per Ex.P.4 clearly discloses that the alleged H/o RTA - hit by bus on 01.09.2023 at 5.15am, the Petitioner has sustained soft tissue injury which is simple in nature.

In Exs.P.7 & 8/
referral slip and OPD Card it is clearly mentioned that A/H/O RTA on 01.09.2023 at 5.15am at Malavalli and the petitioner has sustained pain in the lower back, pain in the Right hip region, head injury/LOC/Vomiting or ENT bleed and abdominal pain.
Chikkaswamy vs K.S.R.T.C on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142660233/
3 12.

The Respondent examined its Driver as RW.1 and got marked Exs.R.1 to R.5 complaint given to PSI, KM Doddi Police Station, Complaint given to DYSP, Malavalli and Maddur Division, complaint given to SP, Mandya, postal receipts and postal acknowledgments.
RW.1 has reiterated the averments of the objections in his affidavit in lieu of his chief examination.
In the cross examination of RW.1, he has admitted that the complaint lodged after 28 days of the accident through RPAD.
The charge sheet is filed against him and he has not challenged the charge sheet.
The Bullock Cart was going from Malavalli towards K.M.Doddi in the same direction.
All the police documents are filed against the Bus Driver.
Moreover the damages suffered by the Bus is also to the front portion.
The photos at Ex.P.11 show the damage to the Bullock Cart.
The sugarcane has fallen on the side of the Road.
There is nothing on record to show the negligence on the part of the petitioner.
Moreover, the attempts by RW.1 to file a complaint of his own as per Exs.R.1 to 3 are his delayed attempts.

Therefore, under these circumstances, appreciating evidence on record this Tribunal is of the opinion that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA- 11-F-0411.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:-

The Petitioner has further averred that on account of the accidental injury he is suffering from Soft Tissue injury which is simple in nature and suffering from pain and agony and also suffered financial loss, since the injuries have caused permanent disability.

The Petitioner to substantiate that there is loss of income due to the accidental injuries and that he is suffering from disability has not examined either the treated Doctor or any other Doctor who has got expertise in this field.
He also has not placed any disability certificate issued by the competent person to prove that he suffered permanent disability.

Therefore, in absence of evidence this Tribunal holds that the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident has not caused him permanent disability resulting in loss of income and accordingly the version of the petitioner in this regard is not acceptable.
Under these circumstances the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income due to disability.
However, it is pertinent to note that, the wound certificate produced as per Ex.P.4 discloses that, he has sustained simple injury.

Exs.P.7 & 8/ Referal slip and OPD Card issued by KM Doddi Hospital and Mandya Institute of Medical Science and Teaching HOspital, Mandya, shows that the petitioner took treatment therein as an outpatient.

sentences.text:
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.25,000/-
under the head of Pain and Suffering.
The Petitioner has stated that he has spent Rs.30,000/- towards medical, conveyance and nourishment expenses.
In this regard he has produced medical bills for Rs.2,350/- as per Ex.P.10.
There is no contrary evidence to this document from the Respondent.
As such, the petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.2,350/- under the head of medical expenses.

As mentioned above the Petitioner was treated at Mandya Institute of Medical Science and Teaching hospital,
Mandya, wherein he was treated as an outpatient.

Mandya
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: During that time, certainly he would have spent some amount towards attendant, conveyance, transportation and for other incidental expenses.

Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards attendant, conveyance, transportation and other incidental Chikkaswamy vs K.S.R.T.C on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142660233/
4 expenses.

The petitioner has also produced the Wound Certificate relating to his Bullocks at Ex.P.4 which shows that one of the animals has suffered femur bone injury and left leg limping and the other has suffered right leg limping and hip bone injury.
The fact of injury to the Bulls and damage to the Bullock cart are also mentioned in the charge sheet.
Therefore, he is entitled to Rs.10,000/- towards medical expenses of the Bulls.
To show the repair charges, the petitioner has produced Quotation and Invoice at Ex.P.9.
There is no contrary admission from him in his cross- examination.
Therefore, he is entitled for a sum of Rs.38,350/- under the head of Repair Expenses.
The petitioner would have suffered loss of his livelihood when the Bullock Cart was being repaired.
During his cross-examination he has stated that he was earning Rs.500/- to Rs.600/- per day from his Bullock Cart.
But we do not know for how many days the Bullock Cart was in the garage.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled to Rs.10,000/- under the head of Loss of Income during repair period.
The petitioner has not produced any document to show that he has sent the Bulls to the GAU-Shala.
Therefore, he is not entitled to any compensation for loss of Bulls.
The total compensation comes to Rs.95,700/-.
If it is rounded off it comes to Rs.96,000/-.
14. LIABILITY:
As discussed above the Respondent has failed to prove its defence about the accident.
Therefore, the Respondent being the RC owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.

The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.10,00,000/- but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.96,000/- along with interest @
6% per annum.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is held in the affirmative.
15. Issue No.3:-

For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition is allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.96,000/- (Rupees  Ninety Six Thousand only) along with  interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
The Respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Chikkaswamy vs K.S.R.T.C on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142660233/
5
The Respondent being the RC owner of the offending vehicle shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within sixty days from the date of this award.
On deposit of compensation and interest, entire amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner through e- payment on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per Rules.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw decree accordingly.
